title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
summary: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

title: On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)
summary: We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bièvre and Torrésani.

title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
summary: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $ν^{es}\otimesν^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
summary: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,μ)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,μ)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.

title: Stark units and cyclotomic Iwasawa theory over complex cubic fields
summary: For cyclotomic extensions of complex cubic fields, we prove the integral rank-$1$ and rational rank-$2$ abelian Stark conjectures. More generally, we prove a relative theorem on the higher-rank Rubin--Stark conjectures for cubic extensions of number fields. We then apply our Stark unit constructions to the Bergeron--Charollois--García conjectures on elliptic gamma values. Finally, we prove an Iwasawa main conjecture relating norm-compatible systems of Stark units to ideal class groups in cyclotomic towers over complex cubic fields.

title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
summary: For a finite dimensional semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the multiplicity $c_{λμ}^ν$ of an irreducible $V(ν),$ inside the tensor product $V(λ)\otimes V(μ),$ of two highest weight irreducible representations can be realised as the dimension of the Kostant--Parthasarathy--Ranga Rao--Varadarajan multiplicity space inside $V(λ)$, $V(μ)$ or $V(ν)$. A result of Panyushev and Yakimova shows how to split the multiplicity space for $c_{λλ}^ν$ inside $V(ν)$ into symmetric and alternating parts when $V(λ)$ is self-dual. For finite-dimensional semisimple or symmetric Kac--Moody, we extend this to Kostant--Kumar modules $K(λ,w,λ)=\mathfrak{Ug}(v_λ\otimes v_{wλ})$ when $w=w^{-1},$ and for all dominant weights $λ.$ We show that the multiplicities of an irreducible in the symmetric and alternating parts of $K(λ,w,λ)$ are given by the dimensions of the eigenspaces of the Tits lift $\widetilde w$ of $w$ on the multiplicity space corresponding to eigenvalues $\pm 1$. This recovers the result for the full tensor product by letting $w=w_0,$ the longest element of the Weyl group. In type A, we also discuss connections to a combinatorial interpretation due to Carré and Leclerc in terms of domino tableaux.

title: Effective bounds for adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer groups of Hilbert modular forms
summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field and let $Π$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb A_F)$. Under the usual Taylor-Wiles residual irreducibility hypothesis, we prove the vanishing of the adjoint Bloch-Kato Selmer group with characteristic-zero coefficients and give an explicit upper bound for a corresponding Selmer group with divisible coefficients. The argument revisits Wiles's use of level raising at Taylor-Wiles primes. In place of freeness or almost freeness of automorphic cohomology over a Hecke algebra, we compare congruence modules at the original and auxiliary levels and control the part of the Hecke cotangent space detected by the automorphic module. This produces Galois cohomology classes with prescribed ramification at the auxiliary primes. The resulting bounds depend explicitly on congruence data at the original automorphic level and on torsion in cotangent spaces of local deformation rings.

title: The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
summary: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

title: Constructing Large Euler Pseudoprimes through Carmichael Products
summary: Inspired by recent work on Carmichael numbers and by the construction of Sanchez, et al., we revisit the subset product construction of Alford, et al. We state a theoretical parallel variant of the pushdown algorithm and extend computational records in two ways. First, we construct a Carmichael number that is an Euler pseudoprime to every base up to $1172819$, which includes the first $90968$ prime numbers. Second, we extend the known list of Carmichael numbers with exactly $d$ prime factors from $d \leq 19565220$ to $d \leq 340210163$.

title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
summary:
For every finite subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincaré pairing on $S^3/Γ$.
  In particular, $Γ$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

title: Cartesian product of $ψ$-badly approximable sets
summary: In this note, we study the Cartesian products of sets in $\mathbb R^{d}$ that are $ψ$-approximable but not $cψ$-approximable for arbitrarily small $c>0$, often denoted $\mathbf{Bad}_{d}(ψ)$. Setting $d=\sum_{i=1}^{N}d_i\in\mathbb N$ and $ψ_i(q)=q^{-τ_i}$ with $τ_i\geq 1/d_i$, $i=1,\ldots,N$, we calculate \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}\prod_{i=1}^{N}\mathbf{Bad}_{d_i}(ψ_i) =\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{\frac{d_i+1}{τ_i+1}+(d-d_i)\right\}=d- \max_{1\leq i\leq N}\left\{ d_i-\frac{d_i+1}{τ_i+1} \right\}, \] for $\dim_{\mathrm H}$ denoting the Hausdorff dimension. The lower bound is obtained by combining the delayed-pruning construction of Koivusalo-Levesley-Ward-Zhang (IMRN, 2024) with the product Cantor-set method of Wang-Wu (TAMS, 2024).

title: Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras
comment: 54 pages, introduction is a preliminary draft
summary:
In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetildeΛ$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $Λ$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$.
  When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.

title: Symmetric identities and determinants for matrices composed of Legendre symbols
summary: In this paper, we prove a series of identities and evaluate the determinants for a class of matrices composed of Legendre symbols given by Sun [10, Conjecture 3.2 (i)]. Together with [6] which proved Conjecture 3.2 (ii) in [10], these results provide a more general approach for a complete proof of Conjecture 3.2 in [10].

title: Murmurations in Short Intervals for Elliptic Curves Ordered by Height
summary: Murmurations are the phenomenon, first observed by He, Lee, Oliver, and Pozdnyakov (2025), that the average value of $ε(E) a_p(E)$, the $p$-th $L$-function coefficient weighted by the root number, over elliptic curves of conductor in some range $N(E) \in [N_1, N_2]$ seem to approximate a continuous, oscillating function. While murmurations have been proven for other families of $L$-functions (notably by Zubrilina (2025) for weight $k$ modular forms), the only unconditional murmuration formula for elliptic curves is a partial result by Sawin and Sutherland (2025) ordering by naive height instead of conductor. In this setting, murmurations appear by first averaging $ε(E) a_p(E)$ for a single curve over $p \in (C_1, C_2)$ and then average over elliptic curves of bounded height. However, Sawin and Sutherland's results average $ε(E) a_n(E)$ over all of $\mathbb{N}$ instead of a small interval $(C_1, C_2).$ In this work, we prove how small the interval $(C_1, C_2)$ can be taken while preserving the conclusion of Sawin and Sutherland's first murmuration formula (Proposition 7).

title: Counting solutions to sparse systems of congruences
summary: We obtain new bounds and asymptotic formulas for the number of solutions to sparse systems of $n$ diagonal congruences modulo an integer $q$ in $s$ variables. In a large range of parameters, our results improve and generalise those of A. A. Karatsuba (1976). In particular, our lower bound on $s$, which guarantees the solvability of such systems, depends only on $n$, rather than on specific degrees as in the work of A. A. Karatsuba (1976).

title: $99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point
summary: When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.

title: Geometric realization of the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in a partially ramified case
summary: We construct a new family of algebraic varieties over a finite field, realizing the local Langlands and local Jacquet-Langlands correspondences for $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in their compactly supported étale cohomology. The resulting representations have $L$-parameters which are induced from characters of a partially ramified field extension.

title: On pseudo-null Iwasawa modules, restricted ramification, and Non-freeness Conjecture over a quartic CM-field
summary: Let $k$ be a CM-field of degree greater than $2$, $p$ an odd prime number that splits completely in $k$, and $Σ$ a $p$-adic CM-type of $k$. In this setting, we show the non-triviality of the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of the maximal multiple $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\widetilde{k}/k$. As a consequence, under a weak form of Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture, we see that the unramified Iwasawa module and the $Σ$-ramified Iwasawa module of $\widetilde{k}$ never coincide. In the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field, under a certain assumption, we show that the non-coincidence condition is equivalent to Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture. We also study a relation of the non-coincidence condition with Non-freeness Conjecture, which is a conjecture studied in non-abelian Iwasawa theory.

title: Counting complex elliptic curves with self-quotients via class numbers
summary:
Let \(n>1\) be an integer. We consider complex elliptic curves \(E\) admitting a finite subgroup \(C\subset E(\mathbb C)\) of order \(n\) such that \(E/C\) is isomorphic to \(E\). % with the additional requirement that the invariant factors of (C) are unequal. We establish class-number counting formulas for the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases.
  More precisely, we associate to every negative quadratic-order discriminant \(D\) the norm form \[ Q_D(x,y)=x^2+\varepsilon_Dxy+q_Dy^2, \] where \[ \varepsilon_D\in\{0,1\},\qquad q_D=\frac{\varepsilon_D^2-D}{4}. \] The invariant factors of the kernel of the corresponding endomorphism are determined by \(\gcd(x,y)\). This leads to finite sets of admissible discriminants describing the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases with unequal invariant factors.
  Our main result expresses the numbers of isomorphism classes in the three cases as sums of the proper ideal class numbers \(h(D)\) over explicitly defined finite sets of admissible discriminants. This provides an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work by \cite{CanepaGaba2014,CanepaGaba2019,CanepaGabaOlteanu2022} and its subsequent algorithmic extensions.
  We also characterize the equal-invariant-factor case: it occurs precisely when $n=m^2$, and in that case every complex elliptic curve satisfies the required condition, with the unique subgroup being $E[m]$.
  We derive an explicit bound for the admissible discriminants, implement the counting procedure in Magma, and give numerical examples. The proof relies on the Smith normal form of the multiplication matrix associated with a quadratic integer.
  The results provide an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work.

title: Deterministic integer factorization from abundance decisions
summary: We prove that deciding whether a positive integer is abundant is equivalent to complete integer factorization under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. In particular, abundance can be decided in deterministic polynomial time if and only if integers can be factored in deterministic polynomial time. Our reduction uses carefully chosen coprime multipliers to recover exact divisor sums from abundance queries, and then extracts the complete prime factorization of an integer $n$ deterministically from the divisor sums of $O(\log n)$ consecutive powers of $n$. Altogether, factoring $n$ requires $O((\log n)^4)$ adaptive abundance queries, each at an integer of $O((\log n)^6)$ binary digits.

title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
summary: We study irreducible trinomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Using an elliptic curve and reciprocity laws, we prove that, for $k \ge 2$, $X^{(4^k+2)/3}+X+1$ is irreducible if and only if $4^k+3$ is prime and $2$ is a primitive root modulo that prime. By power substitution and linearization, we also assemble explicit infinite families of irreducible trinomials $X^m+X^n+1$ in fourteen distinct reduced exponent classes.

title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
summary: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $Γ$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $Γ$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $Γ$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
summary: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by Götze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.

title: On infinite torsion of abelian varieties over large algebraic fields of positive characteristic
summary: Let $A$ be a non-zero abelian variety defined over a finitely generated field $F$. A conjecture of Geyer and Jarden [GJ78] asserts that for every $σ\in \mathrm{Gal}(F^{sep}/F)$ outside a set of Haar measure zero, there exist infinitely many primes $\ell$ such that the $\ell$-torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is non-zero (or equivalently, the torsion subgroup of $A(F^{sep}(σ))$ is infinite), where $F^{sep}(σ)$ denotes the subfield of $F^{sep}$ fixed by $σ$. While this conjecture remains open when $\mathrm{Char}(F)>0$, we establish a new case under the assumptions of $\mathrm{End}(A)=\mathbb{Z}$ and the connectedness of the algebraic monodromy groups attached to $A/F$.

title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta-function: a local multiplicity test and long mixed moments
summary: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that at least 71.274066\% of the nontrivial zeros of $ζ(s)$ are simple, and at least 85.368230% are distinct. The previous bounds were 19/27 $\approx$ 70.37%, due to Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek and to Bui and Heath-Brown (2013), and 84.77\%, due to Chirre, Gonçalves and de Laat (2020). The method combines the two classical approaches to simple zeros. Montgomery's pair correlation argument rests on a pointwise consequence of the explicit formula: at a zero of multiplicity $m\ge2$, a Dirichlet polynomial $J$ over prime powers of length $T^ψ$, $ψ<1$, is forced to have real part at most $-a<0$. The mollified derivative $ζ'(ρ)M(ρ)$ of Conrey, Ghosh and Gonek vanishes there. Both facts are used at the same zero, in a single least-squares inequality. The new analytic input is the mixed moment $\sum_ρζ'(ρ)M(ρ)J(1-ρ)$ with $J$ much longer than the mollifier. We evaluate it under the Riemann Hypothesis alone; the long prime sum stays in the numerator and the mollifier variable is the modulus, so the barrier at $T^{1/2}$ does not arise. A second-order version of the argument gives $0.70736$. We show that no second-order certificate of this type can exceed $0.7073646063$, and pass this ceiling with fourth moments of short Dirichlet polynomials and with mixed moments against products of a bounded number of primes. All constants are certified in exact rational arithmetic.

title: Cohomology of pseudo-reductive groups over local function fields
summary: We give a pairing which describes the first Galois cohomology of a pseudo-reductive group $G$ over a local function field $K$ as the Pontryagin dual of the group $\Ext^1(G, \Gm)$ of translation-invariant line bundles on $G$. In order to accomplish this, we endow the Picard group of a scheme $X$ over a (Hausdorff) topological field with a topology, and prove that this topology enjoys favorable properties under certain mild conditions on $X$ and on the field.

title: A consequence of the classical Lindelöf Hypothesis for the density of zeros of general Dirichlet series
summary: Supposing the Lindelöf Hypothesis for the Riemann zeta function we prove that the density hypothesis holds for Res>3/4 for a large class of Dirichlet series. The first result of similar type was reached by Gábor Halász and Paul Turán in 1969.

title: Non-archimedean generalisations of the Kuznetsov formulas
summary: In this paper we develop non-archimedean analogues of the Petersson-Kuznetsov formulas. Specifically, choosing a particular test function on either the geometric or spectral side of the formula, one may express the other side in terms of integral transforms. Such transforms involve representation theoretic Bessel functions attached to irreducible unitary admissible representations of $\text{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

title: On the equivariant Heegner point main conjecture and refined conjectures of Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer type
summary:
In 1992, Darmon formulated refined conjectures of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer type for Heegner points, and proved the ``order of vanishing'' part of his conjectures by a development of Kolyvagin's Euler system arguments. In this paper, for good ordinary primes split in the underlying imaginary quadratic field, we prove the $p$-part of the ``leading coefficient formula'' conjectured by Darmon, as well as its derived strengthening by Bertolini-Darmon.
  Our method, which also offers a novel perspective on earlier results, is based on the formulation and proof of new equivariant anticyclotomic main conjectures, including an equivariant extension of Perrin-Riou's Heegner point main conjecture.

title: On the Density of Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
summary:
Let $N(a)$ denote the number of occurrences of the integer $a>1$ in Pascal's triangle, and set ${\mathcal E}_H=\{a\geq3:N(a)>2H\}$, $A_H(x)=|{\mathcal E}_H\cap[1,x]|.$ For every fixed $K\geq2$ we prove the expansion $A_1(x)=\sum_{k=2}^{K}(k!x)^{1/k}+O_K\!\left(x^{1/(K+1)}\right).$
  Consequently, the Dirichlet series ${D}_1(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_1}a^{-s}$ extends meromorphically to $\Re s>0$, with simple poles precisely at $s=1/k$, $k\geq2$, of residue $(k!)^{1/k}/k$.
  For every $H\geq2$, $x\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $A_H(x)\le A_2(x)\leq\exp\left(\frac{2\log x}{(\log\log x)^{1/4}}\right)\ll_{\varepsilon} x^{\varepsilon}.$
  Hence $D_H(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_H}a^{-s}$ is holomorphic for $\Re s>0$ when $H\geq2$, and $λ({\mathcal E}_1)=1/2, λ({\mathcal E}_H)=0\quad(H\geq2).$
  Here, for a set $S\subseteq {\mathbb N}$, its exponent of convergence is $λ(S)=\inf\left\{σ>0:
  \sum_{n\in S}n^{-σ}<\infty\right\}.$ We also determine the logarithmic-order counting law for the classical Lind--Singmaster family of coefficients of multiplicity at least six.

title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
summary:
We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property.
  By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.

title: Pairing Powers of Pythagorean Pairs II
summary: Let $(a,b,c)$ be a pythagorean triple, i.e., $a^2+b^2=c^2$. Then $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$ are hypotenuse-leg pairs (hl-pairs), i.e., pairs $(c,d)$ of positive integers such that $c^2-d^2$ is a non-zero square. An hl-pair $(c,d)$ is called a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if there is a pythagorean pair $(k,l)$, which is not a multiple of the pythagorean pair $(d,\sqrt{c^2-d^2})$, such that $(c^hk,d^hl)$ is again an hl-pair. To each hl-pair $(c,d)$ and each $h\geq 1$ we assign the elliptic curve $Γ_{c^h,d^h}: y^2=x^3+(c^{2h}-d^{2h})x^2-c^{2h}d^{2h}x$ and show that its torsion group is $\Bbb Z/2\Bbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ and that $(c,d)$ is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $h$ if and only if $Γ_{c^h,d^h}$ has positive rank over $\mathbb Q$. In this case there are infinitely many such pythagorean pairs $(k,l)$, not multiples of each other. Moreover, every hl-pair is a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $1$ and a pythapotent hl-pair of degree $3$, and we give sufficient conditions for degree $2$. The two cases $(c,a)$ and $(c,b)$, where $a=m^2-n^2$ and $b=2mn$, are worked out separately.

title: On the Distribution of Prime Factors of $\lfloor αn^2 \rfloor$
summary: Let $α> 0$ be irrational. We show that $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ obeys a Gaussian distribution. That is, for $n$ chosen uniformly at random from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, the random variable $(ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor) - \log\log N)/\sqrt{\log\log N}$ converges in distribution to the standard Gaussian as $N$ tends to infinity. Additionally, we fully describe the distribution of $ω(\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ for a positive rational $α$.

title: Sums of Kloosterman fractions and applications
summary: We obtain improved bounds for bilinear and trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, building on the works of Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec and Bettin-Chandee. Our results use the spectral theory of automorphic forms, and save $N^{1/12} A^{1/3}$ over the trivial bound when $M = N$ and $A$ is small. In the exceptional Maass spectrum, we rely on a new large sieve inequality with averaging over the levels, which may be of independent interest. Applications include an asymptotic for the second moment of the zeta function twisted by a Dirichlet polynomial of length $T^{0.532}$ (improving Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill's $T^{0.515}$ and Dong-Robles-Zeindler's $T^{0.518}$), as well as an improved level of distribution for unbalanced convolutions (improving results of Fouvry-Radziwill, Wright, and Dong-Robles-Zeindler).
